title: Become Present
coreMove: Presence means returning attention to the fact, face, breath, or task at hand before fear, memory, or public pressure gets command.

exampleSpecs.audience: Harpreet teaching students how crisis attention works
exampleSpecs.stakes: a learner mistakes presence for a pleasant mood instead of usable attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The learner's confusion about calm becomes the material Harpreet teaches from.

exampleSpecs.audience: Kabir testing whether he can stay with a simple quiet-room exercise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A single quiet-room attempt shows the return move in physical detail.

exampleSpecs.audience: volunteers who confuse pressure with speed
exampleSpecs.stakes: fear may turn future risk into command before facts are checked
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A trainer turns the Kennedy crisis into one plain reframe about staying with available facts.

exampleSpecs.audience: Brock working through a no-dialogue presence exercise
exampleSpecs.stakes: the urge to flee feels like a useful errand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The scene stays inside Brock's thoughts as she catches the wrong turns.

exampleSpecs.audience: volunteers preparing a tense public update
exampleSpecs.stakes: the future can crowd out the person who needs a clear answer now
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A volunteer must choose between rehearsing tomorrow's argument and answering the current person cleanly.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ludivine balancing a message preview and a rare conversation
exampleSpecs.stakes: both options carry a cost, so the next honest act matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ludivine faces one true two-bad-options tension and names both claims before acting.
